# Browser performance

<!-- Generated by scripts/canonical-audit.gen.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Measured in Headless Chromium 140.0.7339.16, desktop CPU (not physical mobile hardware) against a production build, through the shipped worker (`public/vendor/engine.js`) on the full datasets. Each dataset ran in a fresh browser context (empty HTTP cache). “Cold load” is download + gzip decompression + SHA-256 verification + opening the database + the first query; over loopback it measures processing only. “Warm reload” opens the same dataset in a new worker with the file in the HTTP cache. Learn and Practice checks are the exact Check requests (visible data, changed-data fixture, validators and plan checks), every one of which passed.

## First load over a throttled connection

Chrome DevTools network emulation (throughput + latency), fresh browser context per dataset, headless Chromium on a desktop CPU. The time is dominated by download size; once loaded the file is cached permanently (content-hashed URL, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`), and lesson and question pages start the download while the learner reads.

## What was optimised before considering smaller data

- Binary SQLite files (VACUUMed, ANALYZEd, gzip level 9) instead of SQL text seeds, decompressed with the browser’s DecompressionStream and verified by SHA-256.
- One read-only connection per dataset shared by Run and Check; the changed-data check runs inside a savepoint and rolls back instead of rebuilding the database.
- Covering and composite indexes for the access paths lessons and questions use (for example `products(category_id, is_merchandise, list_price)`, `events(account_id, occurred_at)`), and query rewrites where a correlated EXISTS over a window CTE or an unscoped FULL OUTER JOIN was slow.
- Content-hashed asset URLs with immutable caching, and preloading on lesson and question pages.
- Previews of 12 rows (20 for small samples) ship with the page; queries always run on the full data.

No dataset was reduced in scale for performance.
